result.rationale: The diff defines totalPages as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100/50), this yields one extra page, so showingLast (Discourse.computed.propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")) never becomes true on the actual last page and 'next' navigates to an empty page. The math error is directly visible in the diff and affects new pagination behavior.

judged_text: Pagination off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is one too high when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 members / 50 per page gives 3 instead of 2), so showingLast is never true on the real last page, next stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to an empty page; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

record.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one in admin-group.js.es6: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is one too high when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 members / 50 per page gives 3 instead of 2), so showingLast is never true on the real last page, next stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to an empty page; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50 => 3). This makes `showingLast` false on the real last page, so `next` remains enabled. Clicking `next` sets `offset` to `user_count` (see `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `findMembers()` then requests `offset=user_count`, which the server fulfills with an empty members list (`limit(limit).offset(offset)`), producing the empty extra page described. Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (or equivalent) would fix it.
